text:
Aisha (Eng - London): quick question— planning to move from London to Barcelona after my visa renewal in Aug. want to understand: will WFH stipend keep flowing, do i need to switch payroll entity, and does this create any Spanish tax/employer obligations for Redwood?
Rina (People Ops): congrats! :tada: high-level: post-Brexit UK->ES relocation typically requires payroll cutover to Spain once you're tax resident. stipend continuation depends on local policy eligibility. when's your proposed move date?
Aisha (Eng - London): target move-in 2026-09-01. i'll be on a UK dependent visa til 2026-08-31 and then will register as resident in ES.
Jon (Manager - London): fyi i'll approve time off for move week. team fine with overlap.
Payroll UK: note: we need final UK payslip for the last period you were paid in the UK. cutovers we aim for start of month but can support 2026-09-01 if processing timeline allows.
Finance EU: flag: Spain employer registration will likely be required to run payroll and social contributions. small team hires still trigger local employer obligations. we'll run nexus/employer checklist.
Legal EU: also check: if you do client-facing meetings in ES or sign local contracts, that increases permanent establishment risk. but internal product work alone normally doesn't create corporate PE. we'll confirm with counsel.
Aisha (Eng - London): about the WFH stipend: i've been getting £150/month and used it to buy a monitor and ergonomic chair. will that be taxable in Spain?
Rina (People Ops): recurring monthly allowance typically continues if policy covers Spain. one-off equipment reimbursements follow local payroll taxation. in Spain some in-kind benefits can be taxable; we should assume the monitor/desk reimbursement may be taxable if processed after cutover.
Payroll UK: if you submitted UK expenses before cutover we'll treat them on the UK payroll; post-cutover we process on Spain payroll. there can be different net outcomes. we can offer a gross-up if you prefer parity.
Aisha (Eng - London): i'd prefer keeping the UK expense claim as-is and continuing the monthly from Spain.
Rina (People Ops): sounds fine. please attach the expense receipts to your relocation case and tick the "process in current payroll" box.
Aisha (Eng - London): will the move change my benefits (health, pension)?
Rina (People Ops): yes — Spain benefits differ. you'll get a Spain benefits packet and 30-day enrollment window after cutover. UK pension contributions won't carry over; we'll provide local pension/seguridad social details.
Finance EU: if you receive stock or equity exercises, let us know the expected dates — timing across tax residency change matters for tax withholding.
Aisha (Eng - London): good point, i have an upcoming RSU vesting in Oct. but it's below threshold. should i postpone?
Legal EU: RSU timing and residency can affect withholding; Finance/Tax will advise. please flag the vest date in your relocation case.
Aisha (Eng - London): done. submitted relocation form and attached lease intent. PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-5322 created. Assigned to Rina. Reminder: EU payroll cutover SLA 10 business days."
Rina (People Ops): next steps checklist (short): 1) confirm move date 2) upload passport/ID and lease proof 3) indicate which expenses to process in UK payroll 4) provide Spanish bank/NIE when available 5) sign any Spain onboarding docs.
Payroll UK: practical notes: add your UK leaving date in Workday so HMRC reporting is handled. we'll produce final P45-equivalent and coordinate with Spanish onboarding.
Finance EU: we'll run a quick nexus/employer check. Aisha, please confirm you won't be opening client offices or hiring in Spain.
Aisha (Eng - London): no hiring or client contracts planned. purely internal product work.
Legal EU: that reduces PE risk. we'll still loop in external counsel if Finance requests.
PeopleOpsBot: "Reminder: please upload Spanish NIE and bank details within 15 days of arrival to avoid payroll delays."
Aisha (Eng - London): thanks everyone 60a appreciated the quick answers — will ping here if anything changes.
